answer.evidence: The mapping from score to letter is implemented in radon/metrics.py:150-157 (mi_rank): `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`. A score of exactly 9 gives 65+1+1 = C, a score of exactly 19 gives 65+0+1 = B, and a score above 19 gives A. This matches the docstring (A > 19, B for 9 < s <= 19, C <= 9). The boundary behavior is correct but relies on boolean arithmetic, which is hard to read. The tests in radon/tests/test_other_metrics.py:36 generate expected values with a helper, so I would check that the helper is independent of the implementation. radon/complexity.py:15 (cc_rank) is a separate letter mapping for cyclomatic complexity, and it should be checked so its thresholds are not confused with the MI thresholds. radon/raw.py feeds the line-count inputs (LOC/comments) to the MI computation, so I would check those inputs for off-by-one effects near the thresholds. radon/visitors.py supplies the complexity and Halstead inputs and needs only a light pass.
